items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: So I got to be good friends with Buddy Matlock, who later died way too young.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, I can’t come up with his name, the west coast.

Frank Rossolino. Frank did a lot of those lip things that some guys can’t do. Some guys try. I can’t do it. And so you take all these various elements and you mold them into the way you play. I think I’ve done that. But I was madly in love with Abe Lincoln. And Abram Lincoln was a trombone player from Ohio somewhere and ended up recording with Matty Matlock. I got involved with Matty Matlock heavily because I loved his book. This was arranged Dixieland. And I ended up buying most of his library from his son, who…
For Bill to say that, that’s something.
